The search turned up the Playwright 1.60 release notes, which added `locator.drop()`, plus guides on the older upload methods.

- **`locator.drop()` (new in 1.60):** Several sources, including a copy of the 1.60 release text, describe it as a way to simulate dropping external files or clipboard-style data onto an element. It dispatches dragenter, dragover, and drop with a synthetic DataTransfer in the page context, and it works cross-browser. It accepts a `files` option (name, MIME type, buffer) or a `data` option for arbitrary MIME types such as `text/plain` or `text/uri-list` (useful for rich text editors and link-drop components).
- **Version note:** One guide says the Microsoft Playwright API documents locator.drop() from v1.60, so a current release is needed to use it. I didn't reach the official docs directly, so check playwright.dev to confirm.
- **`locator.setInputFiles()`:** This is for a native `<input type="file">`. One guide notes that Playwright sets the selected files without opening the OS file dialog. It also works on hidden inputs.
- **File chooser route:** When a click opens a native dialog without a directly addressable input, you can wait for the `filechooser` event and then call `setFiles()` on the chooser. Set up the wait before the click to avoid a race.
- **`locator.dragTo()`:** This is for moving an existing element within the page, not for dropping files from outside.
- **Drop zones without an input:** Some guides say the older workaround was to build a DataTransfer with a File in the page and dispatch drag events by hand. That approach is what `drop()` is meant to replace.

Several of these sources are third-party blogs, so verify the exact behavior against the official Playwright release notes and API docs.

content.content:
Version 1.60 adds two HAR-related items and `locator.drop()`. The notes don't mention `routeFromHAR`.

**HAR recording on Tracing**
- `tracing.startHar()` and `tracing.stopHar()` expose HAR recording as a tracing API. They take the same `content`, `mode`, and `urlFilter` options as `recordHar`.
- The returned Disposable works with `await using`. The HAR is finalized when that variable goes out of scope.

**`locator.drop()`**
- Simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element.
- Playwright dispatches `dragenter`, `dragover`, and `drop` with a synthetic DataTransfer in the page, and it works across browsers.
- `files` takes `name`, `mimeType`, and `buffer` for each file.
- `data` takes MIME-type keys, such as `'text/plain'` and `'text/uri-list'`.

content.text:
No upgrade is needed. `financial-hq-ui` already runs Playwright 1.60.0: `package.json:129` asks for `^1.60.0`, and `yarn.lock` resolves `@playwright/test`, `playwright` and `playwright-core` to 1.60.0. That is the release that added both of the features you're asking about.

**File drops:** 1.60 adds `locator.drop()`. It simulates someone dragging files from their computer onto a drop zone, and works in all browsers. You pass the files directly:
```ts
await page.locator('.dropzone').drop({
  files: [{ name: 'invoice.pdf', mimeType: 'application/pdf', buffer: fs.readFileSync('fixtures/invoice.pdf') }],
});
```
It also takes a `data` option for things like `'text/plain'` or `'text/uri-list'`. For ordinary `<input type="file">` fields, `setInputFiles()` still works, as it does in older versions too.

**HAR capture:** Recording network traffic to a HAR file (`recordHar` in the context options, `routeFromHAR` for replaying it) has existed for a long time, so any recent version can do it. 1.60 also adds `context.tracing.startHar()` and `stopHar()`. They take the same `content`, `mode` and `urlFilter` options as `recordHar`, and let you record just part of a test instead of the whole browser session. The returned handle works with `await using`.

**What's missing is config, not version:**
- None of the e2e specs use HAR or file drops yet.
- `playwright.config.ts` only saves traces and screenshots on failure. If you want a HAR for every run, you'll need to add `recordHar` (or call the tracing API in a fixture), and send the output into `playwright-artifacts/` so it lands with your other artifacts.
- I haven't run anything. The 1.60 details come from the official release notes; I haven't checked them against the type definitions in your `node_modules`.

Sources:
- [Playwright release notes](https://playwright.dev/docs/release-notes)
- [Playwright 1.60: Drop API, HAR Tracing & Diagnostics (TestDino)](https://testdino.com/blog/playwright-1-60-release)
- [newreleases.io – Playwright 1.60.0](https://newreleases.io/project/pypi/playwright/release/1.60.0)
- [qaskills – setInputFiles guide](https://qaskills.sh/blog/playwright-setinputfiles-file-upload-guide)
- [qaskills – HTML5 drag and drop](https://qaskills.sh/blog/playwright-html5-drag-and-drop-data-transfer)
